arenaMax.description: MALLOC_ARENA_MAX set on every lakehouse container (lance.allocatorEnv) to cap glibc malloc arenas. Default 2.

arrowMemoryPool.description: ARROW_DEFAULT_MEMORY_POOL on every lakehouse container; `system` routes Arrow through malloc so `arenaMax` bounds it.

audit.description: Emit the structured authn/authz/credential-vending audit stream (RASK_AUDIT_ENABLED); takes effect only with auth on. false silences it.

bootstrapAdmin.description: The person's principal (`<idp-id>~<user id>`, e.g. `dex~<userID>`) the catalog grants `owner` on the estate's own warehouse and `admin` on estate:rask from its declaration, moving both when it changes; a bare name fails the render. Empty = no administrator is declared.

enabled.description: Govern the estate: authn on every door plus OpenFGA authz. On by default (fails closed); a bare install then needs `auth.oidc.issuer` or it refuses to render. A real deployment refuses it off.

fgaApiUrl.description: The platform's OpenFGA HTTP API (e.g. `https://fga.internal:8080`), which the tuple writer (the catalog) and the openfga-model hook dial when `openfga.enabled` is false; the render refuses it empty then, and http on a real deployment. It must admit rask's projected `rask-openfga` tokens from exactly the subjects `lance.openfgaSubjects` lists: OIDC against the cluster's ServiceAccount issuer.

fgaEgress.description: NetworkPolicy egress rules ({to, ports}) admitting the pods that dial `fgaApiUrl` (the catalog and the openfga-model hook) to it, at the port a policy sees. Required under networkPolicy.enabled while `openfga.enabled` is false.

fgaStoreId.description: Pin the OpenFGA store id used by every service and the openfga-model hook. Empty = the newest store named `lance-catalog`.

enabled.description: Render the issuer mirror (templates/issuer-mirror.yaml) that republishes the SA issuer's discovery and JWKS unauthenticated for OpenFGA and the development store; off only for a publicly served issuer.

audience.description: The audience every governed door checks (`RASK_OIDC_AUDIENCE`); a client's own id is never it.

audienceScope.description: The scope a client asks the IdP for to obtain a token for `audience`; empty is Dex's cross-client scope, `audience:server:client_id:<audience>`.

clientMarker.description: How the issuer marks a token its client was issued for itself where its `sub` is not the client's id (`RASK_OIDC_CLIENT_MARKER`; `{claim: client_id}` for Keycloak's service accounts, `{claim: idtyp, value: app}` for Entra, an optional claim the tenant turns on, without which its apps read as people); never a claim every token carries; the client is named by the token's `client_id`, `azp` or `appid`. Empty, a token is a client's when its `sub` is the `client_id` it names (RFC 9068).

connectors.description: The idp id each Dex connector's users are principals of, keyed by connector id (`RASK_OIDC_CONNECTORS`; `{ldap: corp}` makes user `u` of connector `ldap` the principal `corp~u`). An idp id is lower-case letters, digits and `-`, never `kubernetes` and never ending in `-client`. With `dex.enabled` and no `subjectClaims` the development Dex's `local` connector is `dex` unless named here. Under it `idpId` names the issuer's clients alone.

egress.description: NetworkPolicy egress rules ({to, ports}) admitting the governed doors that verify a person's token (the catalog, lineage) to the platform's IdP at `issuer` and at each of `providers`, at the port a policy sees. Required under networkPolicy.enabled while `auth.enabled` and `dex.enabled` is false.

idpId.description: The idp id of the issuer's people and clients (`RASK_OIDC_IDP_ID`; `corp` makes the person the issuer names `s` the principal `corp~s` and its client `etl` the machine `corp-client~etl`): lower-case letters, digits and `-`, never `kubernetes` and never ending in `-client`. Empty is `dex` with `dex.enabled`, and required otherwise. It names no rule: `connectors` or `subjectClaims` picks how people are read.

issuer.description: The OIDC issuer every governed door trusts (`RASK_OIDC_ISSUER`; a token is accepted only when its `iss` equals it). Required when `auth.enabled`; https unless `dex.enabled`.

providers.description: Further issuers people and clients sign in at beside `issuer` (`RASK_OIDC_PROVIDERS`), each `{issuer, idpId, discoveryUrl, subjectClaims, connectors, clientMarker}` read as the keys above: an https issuer named once, and idp ids no other issuer names. `egress` must admit each of them under `networkPolicy.enabled`.

subjectClaims.description: The claims a person's subject is read from, the first the token carries winning (`RASK_OIDC_SUBJECT_CLAIMS`); empty is `sub` alone. Name another first where the provider's `sub` is not the stable id a grant needs (Entra's `oid`). Never set beside `connectors`; with `dex.enabled`, setting it reads the development Dex's people by subject instead of by connector.

serviceAccountMaxTokenSeconds.description: The longest lifetime, in seconds, a ServiceAccount token presented at a door may have been minted with (RASK_SA_MAX_TOKEN_SECONDS).

enabled.description: Renders CPU-based HPAs for catalog and lineage, whose Deployments then render no `replicas` (the HPA owns the count). Needs metrics-server; off by default.

maxReplicas.description: HPA maximum replicas for catalog and lineage.

minReplicas.description: HPA minimum replicas for catalog and lineage.

scaleDownStabilizationSeconds.description: HPA scale-down stabilization window in seconds; stops a spiky service oscillating.

targetCPUUtilizationPercentage.description: HPA target CPU as a percentage of the pod's CPU request (not its limit).

dest.description: S3 URI the control-root backup is copied to. Empty writes `_backups/control/` inside the control root itself, which does not survive losing the bucket.

enabled.description: Schedule a CronJob that backs up the control root (project, warehouse and bucket-claim registries). Off by default.

keep.description: Number of newest control-root backups kept after each successful copy; 0 keeps every run.

schedule.description: Cron schedule of the control-root backup (default daily 01:00).

enabled.description: Schedule a CronJob that creates a CSI VolumeSnapshot of the lakehouse PVC; needs a CSI snapshotter and a VolumeSnapshotClass. Off by default.

kubectlImage.description: Image the snapshot job runs; it needs both a shell and kubectl.

schedule.description: Cron schedule of the volume snapshot (default daily 03:00).

snapshotClassName.description: VolumeSnapshotClass the snapshot names; empty uses the cluster default.

periodSeconds.description: Seconds between two ticks of the timer that deletes for good each hidden branch past its deadline (`LANCE_BRANCH_TRASH_PERIOD_SECONDS`).

graceSeconds.description: Seconds a committed version waits before the reconciler looks for its announcement (LANCE_COMMIT_RECONCILE_GRACE_SECONDS): longer than the inline publish and the outbox relay take to deliver it.

horizonSeconds.description: Seconds back the reconciler looks for a version's announcement (LANCE_COMMIT_RECONCILE_HORIZON_SECONDS); kept inside services.lineage.eventsRetentionDays.

periodSeconds.description: Seconds between two ticks of the timer on which the catalog announces every committed version lineage's feed lacks, on each table a door filed a commit for (`LANCE_COMMIT_RECONCILE_PERIOD_SECONDS`).

walkPeriodSeconds.description: Seconds between two walks of every claimed table for a committed version lineage's feed lacks (`LANCE_COMMIT_WALK_PERIOD_SECONDS`).

controlEmit.description: Publish catalog control events (catalog.control.v1) on the catalog's own bus connection, where every replica follows them; declares the CATALOG_CONTROL stream. Best-effort.

enabled.description: Stage control events in a durable S3 outbox and run the relay timer that drains it. Requires `controlEmit`.

periodSeconds.description: Seconds between two ticks of the control outbox relay (`LANCE_CONTROL_RELAY_PERIOD_SECONDS`); bounds how long a control event stays undelivered after a bus outage.
Seconds between two ticks of the timer on which the catalog converges the estate onto `catalog.declared` (`LANCE_DECLARATION_CONVERGE_PERIOD_SECONDS`); lateness only delays a declared change.

grants.description: Grants git declares to principals that are not people, each an entry keyed by a name its values file chooses, `<name>: {object, relation, principal}` (a map, so several values files merge where a list would replace each other's): `object` is `project:<id>` or `warehouse:<id>`, `relation` a rung of that type, `principal` a service account's principal (`kubernetes~system:serviceaccount:<namespace>:<name>`). The catalog revokes a grant removed from here, and only one it wrote from here.

projects.description: Projects git declares, each `{id, admins, protected}`: `admins` lists people's principals (`<idp-id>~<user id>`), and a project naming none is administered by `auth.bootstrapAdmin` when that is set; `protected` arms its deletion protection. The default declares one project, so a one-team install never creates one.

warehouses.description: Warehouses git declares, each `{id, project, bucket, delete_profile, protected, active}`: `bucket` defaults to the id, `delete_profile` is `{mode: hard}` or `{mode: soft, grace_days: n}` (unset takes the estate's grace period), `active: false` deactivates it. The id is the first segment of every name in the warehouse.

deadlineDays.description: Days after an erasure obligation is recorded that it is due; an obligation still open past it is shown overdue (LANCE_ERASURE_DEADLINE_DAYS). Required.

releaseGraceDays.description: Days after an erasure blocked by a tag or branch pin, during which owners are told, before the pins are released (LANCE_ERASURE_RELEASE_GRACE_DAYS). Required.

releasePeriodSeconds.description: Seconds between two ticks of the timer that runs due erasure pin releases (`LANCE_ERASURE_RELEASE_PERIOD_SECONDS`); lateness only costs time.

periodSeconds.description: Seconds between two ticks of the timer that removes each root's `__manifest` versions past retainSeconds (`LANCE_MANIFEST_RECLAIM_PERIOD_SECONDS`); lateness only keeps history longer.

retainSeconds.description: Seconds a `__manifest` version is kept before the reclaim removes it (LANCE_MANIFEST_RETAIN_SECONDS); a dropped id stays readable in the history this long, and the catalog rebuilds each namespace connection after a quarter of it.

maxBodyBytes.description: Maximum request-body bytes on any catalog route (LANCE_MAX_BODY_BYTES); larger bodies get 413 before buffering. Default 256 MiB.

maxConcurrentWrites.description: Cap on concurrent in-flight Arrow-IPC writes; over it the catalog answers 429 + Retry-After. Peak buffer memory is this times `maxBodyBytes`.

dataBases.description: Allowlist of bucket URIs one table's fragments may be spread across (`?data_base=` on create). Empty = multi-base off, single-location creates.

requestDeadlineSeconds.description: Seconds a catalog request may run before its caller is answered 503 (code 17) while it runs on to its end (LANCE_REQUEST_DEADLINE_SECONDS).

trashGraceDays.description: Days, a fraction allowed, a dropped table or namespace stays undroppable, where its warehouse names no delete profile (LANCE_TRASH_GRACE_DAYS). 0 destroys immediately.

enabled.description: Render the console: its Deployment, Service, `/config.json` ConfigMap, ServiceAccount and, with `route.enabled`, its `/` HTTPRoute.

clientId.description: The IdP's public client the console signs in with (PKCE, no secret); the development Dex declares `rask-console` (deploy/fixtures/dex `console`).

scopes.description: Scopes the console asks for; the lakehouse's audience scope is always added, and `federated:id` whenever `auth.oidc.connectors` names a Dex's connectors. `offline_access` asks the issuer for a refresh token, which the console keeps in memory and renews its session with; the issuer must bound it by idleness and by age and rotate it at each use, and one that grants none ends the session at the access token's expiry.

port.description: Port of the console's static server and its Service.

replicas.description: Replicas of the console's static server.

resources.description: CPU/memory requests and limits for the console's static server.

runAsUser.description: The image's non-root uid and gid (`USER 10001` in .docker/frontend.dockerfile), named by number so `runAsNonRoot` can verify it.

enabled.description: This estate uses the development Dex (deploy/fixtures/dex, Service `<release>-dex`): the ingress serves it at /dex, and a real deployment refuses it. The chart renders no Dex.

port.description: Port of the development Dex's Service.

enabled.description: Serves /docs, /redoc and /openapi.json on every app in the release. Off by default; turn on only for a dev cluster.

kubernetesAuthPath.description: Mount path of the store's Kubernetes auth method, which ESO's SecretStore and every service log in through.

kvMount.description: Vault/OpenBao KV mount path the SecretStore reads from.

namespace.description: Namespace of the External Secrets Operator ServiceAccount the Vault role is bound to.

refreshInterval.description: How often each ExternalSecret re-syncs from the store (a duration, e.g. `1h`).

role.description: Vault role the operator's ServiceAccount assumes; also names its read policy.

serviceAccount.description: Name of the External Secrets Operator ServiceAccount the Vault role is bound to, so no other pod can assume it.

forwardedAllowIps.description: Peers whose x-forwarded-* headers uvicorn trusts in every pod the route reaches (--forwarded-allow-ips). Set to the Gateway data plane's pod CIDR; `*` is refused.

fullnameOverride.description: Base name for every rendered object; pinned to `rask` so in-cluster Services resolve as `rask-<component>`.

global.description: Global values shared between all subcharts
global.$comment: Added automatically by 'helm schema' to allow this chart to be used as a Helm dependency, as this schema would otherwise not allow Helm's special 'global' values key.

catalog.description: Lakehouse image (catalog, lineage, maintenance, and the chart's Jobs and hooks): `repository` is its name under image.repository; its tag or digest is `tags`/`digests` keyed by that name, else the global one.

console.description: Console image: `repository` is its name under image.repository; its tag or digest is `tags`/`digests` keyed by that name, else the global one.

digest.description: Global digest pin (sha256:...) for every first-party image; wins over `tag`. Empty uses tags.

digests.description: Per-component digest map keyed by component name; beats `tags` and the global tag.

localImages.description: Renders bare `<component>:<tag>` references for images side-loaded into the node (k3s-import). Never for a remote cluster.

repository.description: Registry prefix for every first-party image (e.g. ghcr.io/<org>/<repo>). Required unless localImages is true.

tag.description: Default tag for every first-party image when no per-component tag or digest is set.

tags.description: Per-component tag map keyed by component name (lance-rest-catalog, web-console); beats the global tag.

imagePullSecrets.description: List of pull Secrets ({name: ...}) added to every first-party pod and hook Job. Empty pulls anonymously.

maintenanceTerminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: Grace period in seconds for maintenance's worker pods, long enough that a stopping worker's running pass finishes (`maintenance.queue.drainSeconds`) rather than being SIGKILLed.

preStopSeconds.description: Seconds every pod sleeps in preStop before SIGTERM, so endpoint removal propagates first.

teardownSeconds.description: Seconds reserved for the app's lifespan teardown; uvicorn's graceful-shutdown bound is grace - preStop - this.

terminationGracePeriodSeconds.description: Grace period in seconds of the pods whose requests answer at no deadline (the console, the issuer mirror); uvicorn's graceful-shutdown bound is this minus preStopSeconds and teardownSeconds. The catalog's and lineage's grace is derived instead: preStopSeconds + their `requestDeadlineSeconds` + teardownSeconds, so every request in flight when the pod is stopped is answered before SIGKILL.

appId.description: Maintenance's app id: its secret-store role (`<release>-<id>`), the bus user its events are published as and its OTel service.

arrivalEnabled.description: Run the write-event lane: queue the written table's pass on each announced commit.

controlEmit.description: Announce each reclamation on the catalog control topic (catalog.control.v1) over the worker's own bus connection. Off by default.

discoveryMaxDepth.description: How deep the bucket walk descends looking for a dataset's `_versions/`; a subtree it stops inside is an IncompleteScan that blocks the purge.

driftRepair.description: Revoke OpenFGA tuples whose object no registry names (ghost projects/warehouses/tables); deletes tuples only. Off by default.

driftRepairDryRun.description: Plan and report drift repair without deleting any tuple. Defaults true.

driftRepairMaxPerTick.description: Maximum objects drift repair revokes per reconcile tick; the remainder is reported as capped and taken next tick.

enabled.description: Deploy the maintenance service (its worker, the hourly audit and the write-event lane).

floorRaise.description: Write one metadata-only commit per stranded table, from its own orphan check, to raise its Lance listing floor so residue becomes reclaimable. Off by default.

floorRaiseDryRun.description: Plan and report floor raises without committing. Defaults true; set false to commit once `floorRaise` is on.

lineageEmit.description: Emit a lineage event per dataset whose versions a pass reclaimed and a FAIL event per errored one; covers every table the catalog's `__manifest` names.

minVersionsToExpire.description: Expiry runs on a table only once it has at least this many reclaimable versions.

olderThanDays.description: Days of version history kept by old-version GC.

ceilingDays.description: The longest a clean or an excluded table goes between two orphan checks, in days: a clean table's interval doubles up to it, and an excluded table waits it. A table whose floor was raised waits its retention and a day, whatever this says.

enabled.description: Run each table's orphan check; off, none is scheduled and one already held ends when it fires.

maxSeconds.description: One orphan check's bound, in seconds, as `queue.maxPassSeconds` is a pass's: past it the check is counted (`maintenance.passes.overran`, kind orphans), and at twice it its replica exits.

ackWaitSeconds.description: Consumer ack wait, in seconds: how long a task a dead worker held waits before another replica gets it. A worker whose heartbeats the bus stops answering ends itself before the ack wait its last answered heartbeat restarted runs out, so its pass never runs beside the next.

auditMaxSeconds.description: The hourly audit's own bound, in seconds, as `maxPassSeconds` is a pass's. It reads one record per table (about 7 ms a table over moto, measured 2026-11-13); keep it under the hour, since an audit still running holds the claim it shares with the scan.

auditSchedule.description: The audit's NATS message schedule (ADR-51): the drift report without the storage walk, its repairs and the lost-task backstop, once per firing on one replica.

commitPassDelaySeconds.description: How long the first commit of a burst holds its table's pass: the most often commits pass a table, each pass covering every commit before it.

drainSeconds.description: How long a stopping worker lets its running task finish, inside its pod's `lifecycle.maintenanceTerminationGracePeriodSeconds`. A pass still running when the drain ends ends its replica, since its heartbeat ends with the drain. The render refuses a drain the grace cannot hold after preStop and the teardown.

heartbeatSeconds.description: How often a running task tells JetStream it is still being worked on; well inside `ackWaitSeconds`.

maxDeliver.description: Deliveries of one task before it is ended and counted (`maintenance.tasks.ended`); the consumer allows one more, on which a task that outlived its worker every time is ended without running.

maxPassSeconds.description: A pass running longer than this is logged and counted; at twice this its replica exits, Kubernetes restarts it, and the task is delivered again.

recheckHours.description: The longest a table goes without a pass: what bounds a lost commit event, and the versions a deleted tag or branch releases.

retrySeconds.description: When a pass that could not decide, or found the table's history held, is tried again.

scanMaxSeconds.description: The daily scan's own bound, in seconds. Its storage walk grows with the estate (three store requests and about 54 ms a table over moto, measured 2026-11-13): past it the scan is counted (`maintenance.passes.overran`, kind scan), and at twice it its replica exits.

scanSchedule.description: The scan's NATS message schedule, a six-field cron (seconds first): the audit with the storage walk, which lists every bucket's directories, then the trash purge its report certifies. Off the hour, so it does not fire with the hourly audit: the two never run at once, and the later one waits out the other's claim.

storeEventsMaxBytes.description: The most STORE_EVENTS holds, in bytes, before it drops its oldest: each event is a hint of about 2 KB that the table's daily recheck backs up, and the stream shares the bus's JetStream disk with LINEAGE and the work queue.

tombstoneSweep.description: Clear trash records whose bytes a probe proves are gone; deletes bookkeeping rows, never bytes. Off by default.

tombstoneSweepDryRun.description: Plan and report the tombstone sweep without clearing anything. Defaults true.

tombstoneSweepMaxPerTick.description: Maximum trash records the tombstone sweep probes and clears per tick; the remainder is reported as capped.

trashPurge.description: Delete the bytes of trash records past their grace deadline and revoke their grants, only when that scan's drift report is clean. Irreversible; off by default.

trashPurgeDryRun.description: Run the purge pass for real but perform no mutation, reporting `would_purge`; adds full read cost.

trashPurgeMaxPerTick.description: Maximum trash records purged per tick; the remainder is reported as capped and drained next tick.

tupleRebuild.description: Recreate OpenFGA tuples the control-plane registries still justify (project admin seed, warehouse tenancy); additive only. Off by default.

tupleRebuildDryRun.description: Plan and report the tuple rebuild without writing. Defaults true.

tupleRebuildMaxPerTick.description: Maximum tuples the rebuild writes per tick; the remainder is reported as capped.

vendWriteCredentials.description: Wire maintenance to the catalog's vending door, the only credential its rewrites are signed with; off, maintenance holds no maintain rung and refuses every rewrite.

port.description: Port a worker pod serves its probes on, for the kubelet.

replicas.description: Replicas of maintenance's worker pods; each runs one worker on the shared work queue.

nameOverride.description: Overrides the chart name used in `rask.name` labels when `fullnameOverride` is empty. Empty uses the chart name.

audience.description: Audience of the ServiceAccount token each session user's pod projects and presents to the bus; the signer's TokenReview names it.

flagged.description: Extra user grants keyed by a values flag path, or several joined by `,` that must all be true, merged into `nats.auth.users` only while the key holds (lance.natsTable).

provisioned.description: Attests the platform's signer admits each session user of `<release>-nats-permissions` and its store holds each static user's `nats-user-<user>`; required when the store is the platform's (`openbao.enabled` false).

sessionSeconds.description: Longest a session the signer grants lives, in seconds: at least 60 and below the projected token's 600 s.

users.description: The bus user table, one user per connection a service opens (named by its app id) plus admin, monitor and object-store, each with publish and subscribe subject lists (never empty); a row supplied by values may name its `serviceAccount` to be a session user.

configMap.description: ConfigMap in the release's namespace holding the CA bundle the bus's TLS certificate chains to, mounted read-only into every pod that connects as a session user. Empty: the system trust store.

key.description: Key of `nats.ca.configMap` that holds the CA bundle.

egress.description: NetworkPolicy egress rules ({to, ports}) admitting the bus's clients (every pod whose service connects to it, the stream Job) to the platform's bus at `url`, at the port a policy sees. Required under networkPolicy.enabled on a real deployment, where the bus is the platform's.

streamMaxAgeSeconds.description: Seconds a message is kept on the LINEAGE, DLQ and CATALOG_CONTROL streams before the stream drops it (max_age).

streamReplicas.description: Raft replica count for every stream the stream Job provisions; must not exceed the bus's node count.

url.description: NATS JetStream address every service and the stream Job connect to (e.g. tls://nats.internal:4222; a comma-separated list for several servers). Required: empty fails the render, and a real deployment refuses any scheme but tls://, whose server must take the TLS handshake first.

apiServerEgress.description: NetworkPolicy egress rules ({to, ports}) admitting the pods that call the Kubernetes API to its endpoints. Required under networkPolicy.enabled while any such pod renders.

enabled.description: Renders default-deny NetworkPolicies with explicit allows and exclusive client lists for the guarded stores. Needs a policy-enforcing CNI.

extraEgress.description: List of extra egress rules, verbatim NetworkPolicy entries, for every pod but the console, to an endpoint no egress value of its own names (the platform's Postgres when OpenFGA runs in the chart). Each rule names its `to` peers; the render refuses one that admits every destination.

objectStoreExtraFrom.description: List of extra NetworkPolicy `from` peers allowed to reach the object store.

openbaoExtraFrom.description: List of extra NetworkPolicy `from` peers allowed to reach the development store (`openbao.enabled`; e.g. the external-secrets namespace).

openfgaMetricsFrom.description: List of NetworkPolicy `from` peers allowed to scrape the in-chart OpenFGA's metrics port (2112): the platform's collector, e.g. [{namespaceSelector: {matchLabels: {kubernetes.io/metadata.name: observability}}}]. Empty admits none.

accessKey.description: Access key id of the store's root account (`rustfsadmin` is RustFS's built-in default id); its secret is `object-store-secret-key` in `<release>-object-store-root`, which only the store and the provisioning hook mount. No workload presents it.

bucket.description: The lakehouse root bucket (catalog `LANCE_REST_ROOT`, warehouse registry, lineage outbox).

buckets.description: Extra platform buckets the provisioning hook creates on the dev store and the reconcile exempts from orphan_buckets; governed data only, not the root or feature buckets.

egress.description: NetworkPolicy egress rules ({to, ports}) admitting the pods that hold a store session (the catalog, lineage, maintenance and its workers, the backup Jobs) to the platform's S3 at `externalEndpoint` and to its STS, at the port a policy sees. Required under networkPolicy.enabled while `enabled` is false.

enabled.description: This estate uses the development object store (deploy/fixtures/rustfs, Service `<release>-rustfs`): rask runs its provisioning hook against it (the platform buckets and every identity's policy), and the dev secret store issues its root credential. Off with `externalEndpoint` set uses the platform's S3. The chart renders no store server.

provisioned.description: Attests that the platform's store (`objectStore.enabled=false`) delivers every object write of every rask bucket (`s3:ObjectCreated:*`) to the bus subject `store.events`, kept through a bus outage; the render refuses a platform store without it.

externalEndpoint.description: S3 endpoint the apps use instead of the development store; pair with `objectStore.enabled=false`. Empty uses the development store. https on a real deployment: the render refuses an http one.

audience.description: The audience every lakehouse workload's store token is projected for, which the object store trusts as its identity provider's client (the rustfs fixture's `identityProvider.clientId`; `sts.amazonaws.com` for AWS). Required.

extra.description: Store identities of the release's namespace outside the lakehouse's own workloads, as `{<ServiceAccount name>: [<policy statement>, ...]}`: each ServiceAccount is rendered with no token mounted, and on the development store the provisioning hook writes its statements as the canned policy its token's subject names, beside the workloads' own, so the hook's prune keeps it. Empty: no other identity holds a store session.

backup-control-root.description: The role the control-root backup's token is exchanged for (`backups.controlRoot`).

catalog.description: The role the catalog's token is exchanged for, for its own IO and every vend.

lineage.description: The role lineage's token is exchanged for.

maintenance.description: The role maintenance's token is exchanged for.

sessionSeconds.description: How long a workload's session lasts (`*_S3_SESSION_SECONDS`, 900 to 43200 s): a service renews its own at half its life, and a backup run asks for one.

port.description: S3 API port of the development store's Service.

enabled.description: Turn on OTLP export from the lakehouse services to `export.endpoint`, and OpenFGA's tracing; needs `export.endpoint`.

environment.description: Value of the `deployment.environment.name` OTel resource attribute; empty falls back to the release namespace.

egress.description: NetworkPolicy egress rules ({to, ports}) admitting the exporting services to the gateway at `endpoint`, at the port a policy sees. Required under networkPolicy.enabled.

endpoint.description: OTLP/HTTP base URL every service exports traces, metrics and logs to (`/v1/traces` etc. are appended): the platform's gateway. Required while `enabled`: empty fails the render, and http on a real deployment.

audience.description: Audience of the ServiceAccount token each service presents on every export; the platform's gateway admits a token for this audience from the cluster's issuer.

lanceLog.description: `LANCE_LOG` on the catalog and maintenance containers: Lance's per-file and per-dataset events, at env_logger's syntax; empty turns them off.

logLevel.description: `RASK_LOG_LEVEL` on every lakehouse container (the catalog, lineage, the maintenance worker, the issuer mirror and the OpenFGA model Job): the level the lakehouse's own loggers write at, to stdout and the OTLP log copy alike. A library's records stay at INFO or above, and the audit trail is armed by `auth.audit`, not by this.

configMap.description: The ConfigMap in the release's namespace holding the CA certificate the platform store's certificate chains to, for a store under a private CA (a trust-manager Bundle's target, for one). Mounted into each service and named to ESO's SecretStore; empty checks the certificate against public roots; refused beside `enabled`.

key.description: The key of `ca.configMap` that holds the CA certificate, in PEM.

egress.description: NetworkPolicy egress rules ({to, ports}) admitting the store's readers to the platform's store. Required under networkPolicy.enabled when `enabled` is false.

enabled.description: This estate uses the development store (deploy/fixtures/openbao, Service `<release>-openbao`): in memory, initialized and seeded by the scripts this chart renders (`<release>-openbao-seed`), its administrator token generated in-cluster. A real deployment refuses it. False reads the platform's store at `externalAddr`.

externalAddr.description: The platform's Vault or OpenBao (https), which the services and ESO's SecretStore read when `enabled` is false; required then, and refused beside `enabled`.

externalReaders.description: A client that reads the store under a role of its own, keyed by its app id `<app>`: `{serviceAccount, secrets}`, its ServiceAccount in this namespace and the secrets its role may read, supplied from the client's own values so the lakehouse names none. An allowlist: a reader holds only `nats-user-<app>`, names of its own (`<app>-<name>`) and `signing-public-<name>`; the render refuses an app id that is no lowercase name, a lakehouse app, one whose own names would cover a store-issued family (`nats-user-<name>`, `signing-key-<name>`, `signing-public-<name>`) or a name a lakehouse identity, ESO, the dev store's seed or another reader holds, or one whose role `<release>-<app>` is ESO's; and a ServiceAccount the lakehouse renders or `default`.

audience.description: Audience of the token projected into each pod for its store login; every app's role accepts only this one.

tokenMaxTtl.description: The store's cap on a token a role issues, at most `1h` and no shorter than `tokenTtl`, in the same forms. A lakehouse service never renews (it logs in again, and its policy grants no renewal); the cap bounds a token an external reader or the secrets operator renews.

tokenTtl.description: Lifetime of the store token a login returns, from `1m` to `1h`, written as `<n>s`, `<n>m` or `<n>h`: the render refuses any other, as a service refuses a login with a lease outside it. A service logs in again once half of it is used and uses a token for at most nine tenths of it.

port.description: Port of the development store's Service.

enabled.description: Renders a PodDisruptionBudget for each service running more than one replica.

database.description: Name of the database OpenFGA keeps its store in.

enabled.description: This estate uses the development Postgres (deploy/fixtures/postgres, Service `<release>-postgres`), and a real deployment refuses it. The chart renders no Postgres. False reads the platform's at `externalHost`.

externalHost.description: Host of the platform's Postgres, which carries OpenFGA's database; the render refuses it empty with `enabled` false while the chart runs OpenFGA, and refuses both set.

port.description: Port of the Postgres OpenFGA and its migrate Job dial.

user.description: Role OpenFGA connects as; its password is the store's `postgres` secret (field `password`), never a value.

topic.description: Topic OpenLineage events are published on and each consumer of them is filtered to (RASK_LINEAGE_TOPIC).

readOnlyWindow.description: Puts the whole lakehouse in a read-only window: the catalog refuses writes and holds its timers, maintenance's worker takes no task, and lineage's relay is held. Flipping it rolls the three services.

catalog.description: CPU/memory requests and limits for the catalog; requests sized so the HPA CPU target is meaningful.

default.description: CPU/memory requests and limits for every lakehouse app container that names no tier of its own (lance.resources).

lineage.description: CPU/memory requests and limits for lineage; requests sized so the HPA CPU target is meaningful.

maintenanceWorker.description: CPU/memory requests and limits for maintenance's queue worker pods (`maintenance.worker`); the web pods keep the default tier.

enabled.description: Renders the HTTPRoutes publishing each `/api/*` prefix, and `/dex` with the development Dex, on the Gateway `parentRefs` names.

hostnames.description: Hostnames the platform's Gateway routes to this release. Required while `enabled` on a real deployment; empty, on a development estate, the routes match every host the Gateway's listener accepts.

parentRefs.description: Gateways the routes attach to, as Gateway API parentRefs ([{name, namespace, sectionName}]). Required while `enabled`.

readOnlyRootFilesystem.description: Read-only root filesystem for every first-party app container; each gets a writable /tmp emptyDir.

tmpSizeLimit.description: sizeLimit of each app's /tmp emptyDir (upload spool, Lance spill, OTel queue); stops one pod filling the node's disk.

appId.description: The catalog's app id: its secret-store role (`<release>-<id>`), its bus user and its OTel service.

module.description: uvicorn import path the catalog Deployment runs (templates/services.yaml).

port.description: Container and Service port of the Lance catalog.

probesPort.description: Container port the catalog answers the kubelet's `/livez` and `/readyz` on, from a thread of its own, so a probe does not wait behind requests (LANCE_PROBES_PORT). On no Service.

replicas.description: Replica count of the catalog. Not rendered while autoscaling.enabled: the HPA owns the count.

requestThreads.description: The most threads the catalog's blocking calls (store reads, Lance commits) run on at once (LANCE_REQUEST_THREADS).

appId.description: Lineage's app id: its secret-store role (`<release>-<id>`), its bus user and its OTel service.

deliveriesInFlight.description: How many of lineage's bus deliveries may be unacknowledged at once (its durable consumer's `max_ack_pending`, and each replica's bound).

ackWaitSeconds.description: The consumer's ack wait, in seconds: how long a delivery a dead replica held waits before another gets it. Lineage cuts a handling 10 s short of it, so the bus never delivers an event beneath a handling still running (LINEAGE_DELIVERY_ACK_WAIT_SECONDS).

attempts.description: Deliveries an event is handled on before lineage parks it (LINEAGE_DELIVERY_ATTEMPTS).

retrySeconds.description: Seconds a delivery lineage asks for again waits before the bus delivers it again (LINEAGE_DELIVERY_RETRY_SECONDS).

eventsRetentionDays.description: Days of arrival time the durable /events feed keeps, pruned on the relay tick; bounds how long a consumer's outage it survives. 0 is unbounded.

key.description: Field of that secret the API key is under.

name.description: Secret in the estate's secret store holding the backend's API key, sent as `Authorization: Bearer`: a secret name (lowercase letters, digits and `-`), since it is a path of lineage's store policy. Empty sends none.

egress.description: NetworkPolicy egress rules ({to, ports}) admitting lineage to the graph backend at `url`, at the port a policy sees. Required under networkPolicy.enabled on a real deployment that sets `url`.

endpoint.description: Path the events are POSTed to under `url` (the transport's `endpoint`).

url.description: Base URL of the graph backend the relay forwards every recorded event to (the OpenLineage HTTP transport's `url`). Empty forwards nothing. https on a real deployment: the render refuses an http one.

maxBodyBytes.description: Maximum request-body bytes on any lineage route (LINEAGE_MAX_BODY_BYTES), one OpenLineage event; larger bodies get 413 before a byte is read.

module.description: uvicorn import path the lineage Deployment runs (templates/services.yaml).

enabled.description: Stages each lineage event to `s3://<objectStore.bucket>/_lineage_outbox` before publishing, drained by the relay. Requires relay.enabled.

port.description: Container and Service port of the lineage service.

probesPort.description: Container port lineage answers the kubelet's `/livez` and `/readyz` on, from a thread of its own, so a probe does not wait behind requests (LINEAGE_PROBES_PORT). On no Service.

provenanceNamespace.description: Namespace the catalog keeps for lineage's feed and edge list (`LANCE_PROVENANCE_NAMESPACE`, `LINEAGE_PROVENANCE_NAMESPACE`): `lance_catalog$<namespace>`, a namespace of the estate's own warehouse; the render refuses any other.

provenanceRetainVersions.description: Versions maintenance keeps of each provenance table: the namespace's keep-last-N policy, written by the catalog at boot (`LANCE_PROVENANCE_RETAIN_VERSIONS`). Null declares none.

enabled.description: Runs the relay's timer in each lineage replica: it drains the lineage outbox, forwards the feed and prunes it.

periodSeconds.description: Seconds between two relay ticks (`LINEAGE_RELAY_PERIOD_SECONDS`); one replica runs each tick.

replicas.description: Replica count of lineage; its replicas share one durable consumer. More replicas add availability, not intake: the catalog bounds it.

requestDeadlineSeconds.description: Seconds a lineage request may run before its caller is answered 503 (code 17) while it runs on to its end (LINEAGE_REQUEST_DEADLINE_SECONDS, ADR 0203).

doors.description: Mode of the bus doors' signature check: "off", "observe" (count would-refuse) or "enforce" (ack and refuse). Always quoted.

provisioned.description: Attest that signing keys exist for every identity in the platform's store; the render fails until it is true there.

encryption.description: Server-side encryption for direct writes, carried in vended storage options: `algorithm` (AES256, aws:kms, aws:kms:dsse) and `kmsKeyId` (kms only, the key ARN under web_identity vending). Empty = bucket default.

endpoint.description: Object-store endpoint every vended credential names (LANCE_S3_VENDED_ENDPOINT). Empty = the catalog's own store endpoint. https on a real deployment: the render refuses an http one.

externalBlobBases.description: Approved external blob bases, each with the warehouse ids whose tables may register a base inside it (LANCE_EXTERNAL_BLOB_BASES). Empty approves none.

mode.description: How the catalog vends storage credentials for direct object I/O: `web_identity` (default, its own token exchanged for a per-table session) or `mode_b` (none, server-mediated).

ttlSeconds.description: Lifetime in seconds of a vended STS / web-identity credential (LANCE_VENDING_TTL_SECONDS).
